triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '1. Treating PDL as tile-level fusion' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 1. Treating PDL as tile-level fusion

problem.statement: SM120 RMSNorm-MLP PDL Pitfalls -- 1. Treating PDL as tile-level fusion

payload.attempted: Enable Programmatic Dependent Launch and expect the consumer GEMM to overlap with producer quantization by tile.
payload.lesson: Use PDL only when the dependency boundary actually exposes useful overlap. Otherwise it is a scheduling mechanism with its own overhead.

established_fact.mechanism: PDL controls launch/dependency timing between kernels. It does not change the stock C1 mainloop into a producer/consumer pipeline.

payload.observed: Whole-A handoff is correctness-safe but only releases C1 after the complete A payload and scale are ready. It does not overlap C1 mainloop with row or tile production.
payload.root_cause: PDL controls launch/dependency timing between kernels. It does not change the stock C1 mainloop into a producer/consumer pipeline.
